question: Can two chat LLM agents cooperate autonomously toward a task from a preliminary human idea with minimal human intervention, and what does the resulting conversation data reveal?
hypothesis: Role-playing with inception prompting lets agents steer themselves to task completion with better solutions than a single-shot answer, and the generated data teaches fine-tuned models new capabilities.
contributions: A novel cooperative agent framework, role-playing, for autonomous collaboration with minimal human intervention
A scalable approach for studying cooperative behaviours and capabilities of multi-agent systems, and the challenges of autonomous cooperation
Demonstration of emergence of LLM training abilities using datasets from four agent collaboration scenarios
Open-sourced library with agents, data generation pipelines, analysis tools and datasets

method.summary: A task specifier agent turns a human idea plus two roles into a concrete task; an AI user (instructor/planner) and an AI assistant (executor), both gpt-3.5-turbo with inception system prompts, converse in instruction-solution turns until the user emits <CAMEL_TASK_DONE> or a termination rule fires. The conversations form the AI Society and Code datasets (plus GPT-4 generated Math and Science QA sets) and LLaMA-7B is fine-tuned on them.
method.task: multi-agent role-playing task solving; instruction-following data generation

inference.max_tokens: conversation capped at 40 messages and by gpt-3.5-turbo token limit
inference.samples: one CAMEL conversation per task; one single-shot gpt-3.5-turbo solution per task; HumanEval pass@k reported for k=1 and k=100 (sampling n not stated)
inference.prompting: inception prompting: task specifier prompt P_T, assistant system prompt P_A, user system prompt P_U; no prompting after conversation starts

parameters.termination: user no instruct for 3 rounds; assistant instructs (role reversal); <CAMEL_TASK_DONE>; token limit; 40 messages max
parameters.critic: optional critic agent (AI or human) picks among proposals, tree-search-like selection (App O)

eval.protocol: Human evaluation: 453 responses collected, anonymised side-by-side, AI Society only. GPT4 evaluation: prompt adopted from Vicuna, scores 1-10 for helpfulness, relevance, accuracy, level of details. No seeds, repeats or significance tests stated.

prompts.text: Here is a task that <ASSISTANT_ROLE> will help <USER_ROLE> to complete: <TASK>. Please make it more specific. Be creative and imaginative. Please reply with the specified task in <WORD_LIMIT> words or less. Do not add anything else.

Never forget you are a <ASSISTANT_ROLE> and I am a <USER_ROLE>. Never flip roles! Never instruct me! We share a common interest in collaborating to successfully complete a task. You must help me to complete the task. Here is the task: <TASK>. Never forget our task! I must instruct you based on your expertise and my needs to complete the task. I must give you one instruction at a time. You must write a specific solution that appropriately completes the requested instruction. You must decline my instruction honestly if you cannot perform the instruction due to physical, moral, legal reasons or your capability and explain the reasons. Unless I say the task is completed, you should always start with: Solution: <YOUR_SOLUTION> <YOUR_SOLUTION> should be specific, and provide preferable implementations and examples for task-solving. Always end <YOUR_SOLUTION> with: Next request.

Never forget you are a <USER_ROLE> and I am a <ASSISTANT_ROLE>. Never flip roles! You will always instruct me. We share a common interest in collaborating to successfully complete a task. I must help you to complete the task. Here is the task: <TASK>. Never forget our task! You must instruct me based on my expertise and your needs to complete the task ONLY in the following two ways: 1. Instruct with a necessary input: Instruction: <YOUR_INSTRUCTION> Input: <YOUR_INPUT> 2. Instruct without any input: Instruction: <YOUR_INSTRUCTION> Input: None. The "Instruction" describes a task or question. The paired "Input" provides further context or information for the requested "Instruction". You must give me one instruction at a time. I must write a response that appropriately completes the requested instruction. I must decline your instruction honestly if I cannot perform the instruction due to physical, moral, legal reasons or my capability and explain the reasons. You should instruct me not ask me questions. Now you must start to instruct me using the two ways described above. Do not add anything else other than your instruction and the optional corresponding input! Keep giving me instructions and necessary inputs until you think the task is completed. When the task is completed, you must only reply with a single word <CAMEL_TASK_DONE>. Never say <CAMEL_TASK_DONE> unless my responses have solved your task.

You are a <CRITIC_ROLE> who teams up with a <USER_ROLE> and a <ASSISTANT_ROLE> to solve a task: <TASK>. Your job is to select an option from their proposals and provides your explanations. Your selection criteria are <CRITERIA>. You always have to choose an option from the proposals.

We would like to request your feedback on the performance of two AI assistants in response to the user question displayed above. Please rate the helpfulness, relevance, accuracy, level of details of their responses. Each assistant receives an overall score on a scale of 1 to 10, where a higher score indicates better overall performance. Please first output a single line containing only two values indicating the scores for Assistant 1 and 2, respectively. The two scores are separated by a space. In the subsequent line, please provide a comprehensive explanation of your evaluation, avoiding any potential bias and ensuring that the order in which the responses were presented does not affect your judgment.
prompts.where: App H, p29 (system prompt: You are a helpful and precise assistant for checking the quality of the answer.)

prompts.text: You are an experienced solution extracting agent. Your task is to extract full and complete solutions by looking at the conversation between a user and an assistant with particular specializations. You should present me with a final and detailed solution purely based on the conversation. You should present the solution as if its yours. Use present tense and as if you are the one presenting the solution. You should not miss any necessary details or examples. Keep all provided explanations and codes provided throughout the conversation. Remember your task is not to summarize rather to extract the full solution.

limits: Evaluation uses GPT4 and humans who may prefer longer answers; authors concede "Human evaluators may have a preference for longer answers" (K.1).
Baseline is a single-shot gpt-3.5-turbo answer and a zero-shot-CoT variant; CAMEL conversations use many more calls and tokens, and the cost is not compared.
CAMEL solutions are summarised by GPT4 before judging, so the summariser adds capability and the comparison is not output-for-output.
Human evaluation covers AI Society only; code was judged by GPT4 only.
No seeds, repeats, confidence intervals or significance tests; decoding settings (temperature etc.) not stated.
Only two-agent setting studied; more than two agents and competition left to future work.
Fine-tuning gains come from GPT-generated data (distillation from gpt-3.5-turbo/GPT4); LLaMA licence and OpenAI terms restrict use to research.
Misalignment/malicious-use risk shown by an example (hacker and AGI), no quantified safety result.
Text-to-judge winner tables for Table 2 scrambled in cache; role selection was manual for the trading example; embodied agents and critic-in-the-loop are shown as examples only with no numbers.
Models are from early 2023 (gpt-3.5-turbo, LLaMA-7B, Vicuna); HumanEval numbers have dated.

terms.definition: cooperative agent framework in which an AI user and an AI assistant, given roles and a specified task, converse in instruction-following fashion until the task is done
prompt engineering occurs solely at the beginning (task specifier, assistant system, user system prompts); then the two agents prompt each other automatically in a loop until termination
agent that turns a preliminary idea into a specific task; an enhanced imagination module
a critic agent (AI or human) selects among proposals or gives feedback, enabling tree-search-like decision-making
assistant reply of the form "I will..." that promises action without taking it
